chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Whichever woman sees the purity (end of menstruation) while she is able to perform the ritual bath (ghusl) during the time of a prayer, but she delays it until the time for another prayer enters, then upon her is the making up (qada) of that prayer which she delayed; and if she sees the purity during the time of a prayer, so she rises to prepare for it, and the time of that prayer passes and the time for another prayer enters, then there is no making up for it upon her, and she should pray the prayer whose time has entered.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed prayers if a woman delays her ritual bath after menstruation ends?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between negligent delay and natural progression of time regarding the ritual bath (ghusl) after menstruation, establishing that missed prayers are only obligatory if the delay was due to the woman's own procrastination. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the obligation to pray is tied to the entry of its specific time, and the bath is a prerequisite condition rather than a time-bound act itself. This ruling ensures fairness by not penalizing women for the time required to perform purification when they are actively engaged in the process.
